items: The IMF reaches a staff-level agreement on Egypt's final EFF review and third RSF review, worth about $2.3 bn → board approval before 15 December would close the programme and support the pound and Egypt's credit standing.
Egypt's economy grows 4.9% in July to September, up from 4.7%, while unemployment rises to 6.0% → growth holds up despite the war, rate hike and gas cuts.
Orascom Construction's nine-month profit nearly doubles to $218 mn as its backlog reaches $11.6 bn → strong awards support the stock ahead of the OCI merger listing on 24 November.
Gold falls 3.2% on Wednesday to its lowest close since September 2025; 21K in Egypt drops to EGP 5,750 → Fed minutes show almost all officials see more hikes ahead.

Misr Insurance Holding will sell 15% of Misr Life Insurance on the EGX in December, with EFG Hermes as sole bookrunner → the IMF wants about $1.5 bn of asset sales before the programme ends; Banque du Caire has delivered $658 mn so far.
EGX30 falls 0.99% to 51,682 on Tuesday and the EGX70 drops another 2.42% → local investors are the sole net sellers as small caps extend their slide.
Gold drops below $3,800 as Fed officials signal more rate hikes; 21K gold in Egypt slips to EGP 5,900 → higher US yields and a firm dollar weigh on bullion and on emerging-market carry.
The Arab Energy Fund files a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → Gulf money keeps buying into EGX-listed energy services.

Seven fertiliser makers agree to pay 50% more for gas, $12.75 per mmBtu and $175 mn upfront, in return for exporting their full output until early January → the state recovers some LNG costs while producers keep selling urea at about $535 a tonne; gas cuts of 20-40% stay.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,200 on Monday but the EGX70 drops 3.76% and the EGX100 2.88% → small caps sell off while Edita (+7.4%) and Telecom Egypt (+5.2%) hold up the blue-chip index.
Edita posts record quarterly revenue of EGP 7.3 bn, up 32.9%, with profit up 41.5% → volume growth and pricing lift the snack maker, and the stock jumps 7.44%.
Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd move three more Gemini services back to the Suez Canal from December → more Asia-Europe traffic adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.

Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027, covering about 26.5 mn workers → higher wages lift consumer spending but raise costs for labour-heavy industries.
TMG Holding's nine-month profit rises 11.9% to EGP 11.72 bn, Fawry's 32% and Edita's 54% → earnings season keeps delivering growth for EGX blue chips.
ONE's container ship crosses the Suez Canal and three more Premier Alliance services are set to follow → the return of Asian carriers adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.
EGX30 rises 0.31% to 52,187 on Sunday, led by Orascom Construction (+3.4%) and AMOC (+4.8%) → the index is up 24.8% this year, though turnover runs 17% below its 90-day average.

Egypt's final IMF review moves to virtual talks with about $2.3 bn at stake before the programme ends on 15 December → the Cairo mission ended without a staff-level deal; a miss would delay funds and could unsettle the pound.
Telecom Egypt's nine-month profit jumps 43.7% to EGP 24.38 bn and Elsewedy Electric's rises 20.7% to EGP 15.30 bn → two large listed companies report strong growth ahead of Sunday's session.

An ENGIE-led group with Orascom Construction closes $588 mn of debt for a 900 MW wind farm at Ras Shokeir → the project doubles the group's wind capacity in Egypt and gives Orascom a construction contract.
Iran says it targets a US base in Bahrain again as Saudi forces down Houthi drones; Brent ends the week at $96.13 → Gulf attacks keep oil high and Egypt's energy bill under pressure.

stories.h: AI sell-off spreads from Wall Street to Asia despite Anthropic's record IPO
stories.what: The Nasdaq Composite falls 2.3% and the S&P 500 2% on Thursday. On Friday Seoul's Kospi drops 5.4%, Taiwan's Taiex more than 6.8% and Tokyo's Nikkei as much as 4.9%. Anthropic's shares rise 17% on their Nasdaq debut after an $81.3 bn IPO, which Al Jazeera calls the largest in history. Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigns with no named successor, and its shares fall 12.8% over the week, EnterpriseAM reports.
stories.aff: Global equities, tech stocks and risk appetite.
stories.eg: A global risk-off mood can slow foreign flows into Egyptian assets.
stories.egx: Bearish for sentiment at Sunday's open.

key.l: monthly private-sector minimum wage from 1 Jan 2027

stories.h: Private-sector minimum wage rises 21% to EGP 8,500
stories.what: The National Wages Council approves raising the private-sector minimum wage to EGP 8,500 a month from EGP 7,000, effective 1 January 2027. It covers about 26.5 mn workers and is the first increase since March 2025.
stories.why: EnterpriseAM gives no reason; October urban inflation is 12.7%.
stories.aff: Household incomes and company payroll costs.
stories.eg: More spending power for workers, higher costs for employers.
stories.egx: Bullish for consumer staples; mixed for labour-heavy industry.
stories.names: Edita, Juhayna (bullish); textiles and manufacturing (sectors, cost risk).

stories.h: EGX30 slips 0.17% as Telecom Egypt falls
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 0.17% to 51,458.04 on Thursday, its third straight loss, and the EGX70 0.33%; market cap is EGP 4.06 tn. Turnover is EGP 6.2 bn, 43.9% below the 90-day average. Edita (+2.94%) and Emaar Misr (+2.32%) gain, while Telecom Egypt (-3.47%) and Orascom Construction (-1.93%) fall.
stories.why: The sources give no single cause; the index is up 23.0% this year.
stories.eg: Thin turnover shows caution before the weekend.
stories.names: Edita, Emaar Misr (up); Telecom Egypt, Orascom Construction (down).

key.l: spot gold, Fri 20 Nov at 06:27 GMT

stories.h: Gold slides to a 14-month low as markets bet on a December Fed hike
stories.what: Spot gold falls 1.9% to $3,554.19 on Friday after touching $3,513.54, and is set for a 9% weekly drop. CME FedWatch shows a 97.3% chance of a 25 bp Fed hike in December. On Thursday gold fell 2.6% to $3,627.46. In Egypt, Banky's latest 21K price is EGP 5,750 a gram.
stories.why: Rate-hike bets, a strong dollar and margin-call selling weigh on gold.
stories.eg: Cheaper gold for Egyptian buyers; Banky's prices may fall further.

stories.h: Oil edges up after a Houthi attack on Riyadh and mine hits in Hormuz
stories.what: Brent rises 0.9% to $92.77 on Friday after settling up 3 cents at $91.98 on Thursday; WTI settled at $83.21, its lowest since 26 August. Houthi missiles target Riyadh, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards report two tankers hit by mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent is still set for a 3.5% weekly fall.
stories.why: Gulf attacks offset a supply surplus as Hormuz shipments return to near pre-war levels.
stories.eg: Brent near $93 keeps Egypt's energy costs steady.

key.l: stake of Misr Life Insurance to float

stories.h: Misr Life float set for next month; Amea Power signs $850 mn wind deals
stories.what: Misr Insurance Holding, owned by the Sovereign Fund of Egypt, plans to float 15% of Misr Life Insurance on the EGX next month by selling 750 mn existing shares. Amea Power signs $850 mn in contracts with PowerChina and Mingyang for a $650 mn, 500 MW wind farm at Ras Shukeir and a $200 mn turbine factory in the SCZone.
stories.why: The IMF wants faster state asset sales; Egypt needs more power.
stories.aff: The EGX's depth, state divestments and renewable energy.
stories.eg: A new large state listing and foreign investment in power.
stories.egx: Bullish for market depth and the state IPO pipeline.
